scope: Ukraine · civil and criminal procedure (separately scoped references)

expert_role.basis: Criminal: КПК ст. 69, 101–102, 242–244; civil: ЦПК ст. 72, 102–106. Appointment requirements depend on the proceeding.

esig_regulation.basis: Law 2155-VIII, Article 18(5)-(7); qualified status requires the applicable certificate, service and signature-validation conditions.

timestamp_recognition.basis: Law 2155-VIII, Article 26: qualified time/date and integrity presumptions.

evidence_rules.basis: Sources, relevance, admissibility and assessment of evidence; Articles 86–87 address lawful collection and serious rights violations.
Documents can include computer data and recorded sound or images. Original/copy requirements and the conditions in Article 99 still apply.

Covert investigative actions have separate authorisation and procedural requirements; Article 252 addresses recording results and Article 256 their evidential use. A software archive does not supply those authorisations.
Distinguish a court-appointed expert from a party-commissioned opinion; the latter states its court-submission purpose and the expert's awareness of false-opinion liability.

sources.term: Electronic Identification and Electronic Trust Services, Law 2155-VIII

review_updates.scope: Added criminal evidence references and trust-service provisions from official indexed Rada texts. This is a reference subset, not a complete review of authorisation, admissibility, wartime exceptions or local court practice.
